subject.title: [Feature]: Support Anthropic native server-side tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution)

question: What Anthropic native server-tool surface should OpenClaw support first, and what security/default boundary should govern code_execution/PTC and web_fetch/web_search replay?
rationale: Current source clearly lacks the requested feature, but the right shape affects provider plugin contracts, config compatibility, billing visibility, encrypted content replay, and a server-side code execution boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design a provider-owned server-tool contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker and ask the Anthropic/provider owners to define an explicit plugin/transport contract covering web_search, web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, allowed_callers, replay, docs, tests, and security defaults.

options.title: Land only native web_search first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49949 as the immediate implementation path and defer web_fetch/code_execution/PTC to separate follow-ups after a narrower provider contract exists.

options.title: Decline server tools for now
options.body: Document that OpenClaw will keep managed web_search/web_fetch and local/provider code_execution paths until server-tool replay and security semantics are mature enough.

recommendation.title: Design a provider-owned server-tool contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker and ask the Anthropic/provider owners to define an explicit plugin/transport contract covering web_search, web_fetch, code_execution/PTC, allowed_callers, replay, docs, tests, and security defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already provided the keep-open review on this tracker and recent history ties him to Anthropic provider/runtime boundary work.
